title: Phase control of magnon-phonon coupling via magnetic field
authors: Yasuhiro Todaka, Motoki Asano, Isamu Yasuda, Masashi Kawaguchi, Daiki Hatanaka, Masamitsu Hayashi
abstract: We study the phase of the coupling between magnons and surface acoustic wave (SAW) phonons in magnetic thin films. The coupling constant changes from a real to a complex number as the external magnetic field is reduced. Below a transition field, the imaginary coupling constant allows SAW phonons to couple to overdamped magnons whose resonance frequency is close to zero and far from the SAW resonance. The strength of the imaginary coupling constant and the magnitude of the transition field both scale with magnetic damping. We find the coupling produces a broad, pronounced minimum in the SAW transmittance spectrum near zero magnetic field in a Ni/Ru/Ni synthetic antiferromagnet with large magnetic damping. These results demonstrate that the phase of the complex magnon-phonon coupling constant can be tuned via magnetic field in strongly damped magnets, offering a platform to explore novel regimes of magnon-phonon interactions.
summary: This work demonstrates phase control over magnon-phonon coupling in magnetic thin films by varying an external magnetic field. By tuning the coupling constant's phase from real to complex, the system can couple to overdamped magnons. This mechanism is experimentally observable as a distinct minimum in the SAW transmission spectrum near zero magnetic field.
main_problem: The study investigates how the phase of the magnon-phonon coupling constant can be controlled by tuning an external magnetic field in magnetic thin films.
main_result: The phase control allows for coupling to overdamped magnons via an imaginary coupling component ($\Phi = -\pi/2$), which manifests as a pronounced minimum in the SAW transmittance spectrum near zero magnetic field.
method: The research combines theoretical modeling using coupled equations of motion (LLG and elastic wave equations) with analysis of measurable quantities like SAW transmittance.
model_or_system: The system is a magnetic thin film, specifically a Ni/Ru/Ni synthetic antiferromagnet, where magnons interact with surface acoustic waves (SAW) phonons.
key_observables: SAW transmittance ($\lvert S_{21} vert^2$), the phase ($\Phi$) of the coupling constant, and the magnon eigenfrequency ($\omega_m$).
important_parameters: External magnetic field ($\mu_0H$), magnetic damping ($\alpha$), and the transition field ($H_{tp}$).
main_assumptions: Initial analyses neglect magnetic anisotropy and magnetic dipole interactions, though later work incorporates these effects.
figures_summary: Figures show the dependence of SAW transmittance on magnetic field, illustrating dips associated with both $\Phi=0$ and $\Phi=-\pi/2$ coupling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the coupled equations of motion, analyzes the complex nature of the coupling constant, and then calculates the resulting SAW transmittance spectrum under varying magnetic field conditions.
why_interesting: The ability to tune the coupling phase via magnetic field provides a clean platform to explore non-Hermitian physics and dissipative coupling mechanisms in solid-state magnonics, relevant to open quantum systems.
